newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: No Australia media policy announcement seen Tues.
newsitem.headline: No Australia media policy announcement seen Tues.

text.p: The Australian government is not expected to announce a decision on media ownership policy after a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, a government official said.
"No submission was taken before cabinet," the political official said. Proposed policies must be formally submitted.
The government is reviewing the so-called cross-ownership rules, which prevent the owners of a newspaper from owning a television station in the same market.
Australia's second-largest newspaper group, John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, is widely expected to be the target of a bid by media proprietor Kerry Packer if the rules are loosened.
Packer controls television stations through his listed vehicle, Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
Fairfax shares, which have risen strongly on the bid talk in recent sessions, closed a cent lower at A$3.24 on Tuesday.
PBL shares closed seven cents down at A$6.38 in a stronger overall market.
